title: SLO acceptance criteria and cross-org gate checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working draft of acceptance criteria and a gate-checklist to be used when teams propose new SLOs or change existing SLOs for model-serving services. The goal is to have a lightweight, repeatable gating process that ensures cross-functional readiness (SRE, Platform, Product, Observability, Security) before SLOs are declared and enforced.

Audience:
- Service owners (product + eng)
- Oncall and SRE partners
- Observability and Alerting engineers
- Platform and infra owners (autoscaling, capacity)

Principles (short):
- Keep gates as small as possible but sufficient to avoid obvious regression risk.
- SLOs are product-facing contracts; include product sign-off.
- Prefer experimental SLOs (90-day pilot) before long-term commitments.
- Make measurement windows, error definitions, and alert thresholds explicit.

Top-level checklist (pass/fail gates):
1) Ownership & contactability
   - Service owner identified (name and email) - REQUIRED
   - Oncall rotation updated to include service oncall alias - REQUIRED
   - Escalation path documented in team runbook - REQUIRED

2) Definition clarity
   - Clear SLI definition (exact metric, numerator, denominator) e.g., "successful_text_generation / total_requests with 1s tail cutoff" - REQUIRED
   - Measurement window(s) documented (rolling 7d/30d) - REQUIRED
   - Latency buckets and p50/p95/p99 definitions included where relevant - REQUIRED

3) Observability readiness
   - Dashboard template created and accessible to SRE and product - REQUIRED
   - Synthetic / canary checks implemented that exercise the critical path - STRONG RECOMMENDATION
   - Alerts defined (page vs ticket) with runbook links - REQUIRED for page alerts
   - Alerting noise sanity check (expected daily alert rate < 1 per team during steady-state) - EXPECTED

4) Alert policy & oncall impact
   - Burn-rate policy agreed (e.g., 14-day burn for major SLOs) and encoded in alerting rules - REQUIRED
   - Temporary suppression plan during rollout (how to mute non-actionable flaps) - REQUIRED

5) Capacity & failure domains
   - Capacity plan for expected QPS under SLO target (headroom % documented) - REQUIRED
   - Fallback model/variant and routing policy for graceful degradation documented - REQUIRED if model variants exist
   - Cross-region failover test scheduled (if multi-region) - RECOMMENDED

6) Deployment & change control
   - Canary experiment plan with success criteria (traffic %, duration, metric checks) - REQUIRED
   - Rollback criteria explicit (metric thresholds or error patterns) - REQUIRED
   - Release runbook and pre/post-check commands included - REQUIRED

7) Data privacy & compliance
   - Any PII/tagged input handling verified with Security & Compliance (KMS, logs scrubbed) - REQUIRED for private deployment customers
   - Audit logging enabled for decisions that affect degradation or bypassing SLOs - RECOMMENDED

8) Risk assessment & mitigation
   - Top 3 failure scenarios and mitigations summarized (e.g., KV cache thrash -> circuit-breaker config) - REQUIRED
   - SLO rollback path (how to revert SLA declarations if necessary) - REQUIRED

9) Stakeholder sign-offs
   - Product: acceptance of customer-facing contract text - REQUIRED
   - SRE: operational readiness signoff - REQUIRED
   - Observability: dashboards & alerts reviewed - REQUIRED
   - Security/Compliance: signoff if relevant - CONDITIONAL

Example SLO acceptance template (to be copied into PR):
- Service: text-gen-api
- Owner: @service-owner (email)
- SLI: successful_response_with_prompt_hash / total_requests (status code 200 AND finish_reason != "error")
- Window: rolling 30d; target: 99.5%
- Latency: p95 < 350ms on inference-only path
- Canary: 1% traffic for 48 hours with automated checks on p95, error rate < 0.1%
- Dashboards: /dashboards/text-gen-api-slo (owner: observability)
content_addendum:
Operational run-through steps (playbook excerpt):
A) Pre-deploy (team): run local synthetic harness against canary image; validate KV cache warm-up; confirm throughput under expected batch sizes.
B) Canary (platform): deploy to canary pool; route 1% traffic; monitor synthetic and real traffic for 48h; watch for surge in retries or latency tail.
C) Roll-forward: increase in 5x steps, validate no increase in page alerts and burn-rate.
D) Post-roll: update SLO docs, disable temporary suppressions, notify stakeholders.

Unresolved questions (please comment inline):
- Should we standardize on 30d rolling windows for all customer-facing SLOs or allow product exceptions? (pro: stable; con: slower to react)
- What is the acceptable daily alert volume envelope per service before we flag an alerting design problem?

Action items (owners + dates):
- Create SLO PR template in repo (owner: Marcus Li) - due 2026-03-09
- Implement canary synthetic harness starter kit (owner: Ethan Morales) - due 2026-03-16
- Draft product-facing SLO language for critical public endpoints (owner: Priya Kapoor) - due 2026-03-12
- Run two pilot SLOs using this gate in April (owners: Clara Zhang + SRE leads) - kickoff 2026-04-01

Decision log snapshot:
- 2026-02-25: agreed to require dashboard + alert spec for SLO acceptance (vote: SRE + Observability + Product = unanimous)
- 2026-02-27: agreed to recommend 7d and 30d rolling windows; default to 30d for published SLOs (action: document exemptions)

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally terse; the goal is to provide checklistable items that service owners can tick off. Feedback: if an item is blocking too many teams, propose an exemption mechanism with clear compensating controls.
- Put any comments on the PR linked in linked_artifacts or ping #sre-slo on Slack.

References & helpers:
- SLO PR template (linked_artifacts)
- Observability dashboard template: /dashboards/templates/slo-overview
- Alerting example: github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/rules/examples/slo-burn.yaml

Last edit notes:
- 2026-03-02: tightened the observability gate to require a dashboard and synthetic checks; added action items for pilot runs.

---
End of draft.
